newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat seeding nearly complete.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat seeding nearly complete.

text.p: Seeding of Kansas's wheat crop was nearly complete during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
A widespread frost late in the week should stop the growth of fall crops and help dry down grain.
The report said producers intend to seed additional acreage in the east central and south central districts, where wet conditions have so far prevented completion.
Wheat seeding was 98 percent complete, on par with average but lagging 100 percent a year ago. Wheat was 95 percent emerged, versus 89 last year and the average of 87 percent.
Wheat was rated 91 percent good to excellent and nine percent fair.
Corn was 93 percent harvested versus 81 at this time last week, 94 last year and the average of 90 percent.
Sorghum was 77 percent harvested, versus 58 last week, 91 last year and the average of 78 percent. Soybeans were 82 percent harvested, versus 73 last week, 94 last year and 89 on average.
Pasture condition was rated 74 percent good to excellent, versus 76 at that level last week.
